Rendered from `tmvp help` and `tmvp <command> --help` at build time.

## tmvp
```text
tmvp reads postgres/k8s/nats/... across every env of one product.

  tmvp all db query "select 1"          # every env that has db
  tmvp prod,staging db describe users
  tmvp '*.db' health                      # selector: any env, system db
  tmvp prod -l role=primary health        # label selector
  tmvp write prod db "update ..." --reason "fix #42" [--preview]

Usage:
  tmvp [envs|all|selector] <system> <verb> [args] [flags]
  tmvp [command]

Available Commands:
  certs       TLS cert expiry of every system's endpoint + certs held in secrets (warn < --days, fail if expired)
  check       Validate config, resolve secrets (names only) and connect to every selected system
  code        Code Mode: run ONE JS program that calls tmvp operations (<system>.<verb>) in-process; only its final JSON returns
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  config      Inspect the config
  doctor      What is installed, what can I connect to, what is broken (works without a config)
  env-keys    List variable NAMES in every .env / .env.<env> / <env>.env under dir (default .), grouped by env; values are never printed
  envs        List envs: destructive flag and system count (config only; no secrets, no server)
  export      Print pg_service.conf / kubeconfig snippets for plain psql/kubectl (never secret values)
  help        Help about any command
  llms        Print the agent docs: llms.txt index, one topic (config, writes, postgres, …), or everything
  login       Show login status; for web systems with manual: browser, open the headed login
  logs        Read back the product's event log / write audit
  new         Scaffold things (new skill <product>)
  secrets     Manage and check the server's in-memory secrets for this product
  server      The local tmvp server (auto-started by every call)
  skill       Product skill: add <name> <type>, sync (SKILL.md from config), lint; install (shipped skills like tmvp-discoverer)
  systems     List systems per env: name, type, labels, via, login (config only; --check runs the login checks)
  use         Show or set the active env for this product (TMVP_ENV and -e override it; `default` or --clear resets to default_env)
  validate    Validate the config: schema, refs, name collisions, via cycles, literal secrets (runs no secret command)
  verbs       List the verbs of each connector type (mode: read | write | destructive | read-write)
  version     Print version, protocol and registered connector types
  write       Run one mutation on one env/system (audited; --reason required; protected envs also need --force)

Flags:
      --config string     config file (overrides lookup order)
      --diff              only show rows/lines where envs disagree
  -e, --env string        env selector: dev | dev,prod | all | 'prod*' (overrides TMVP_ENV, tmvp use, default_env)
      --force             reads: run even if the estimate exceeds the timeout (timeout still kills); writes: required for a protected env
  -h, --help              help for tmvp
      --json              JSONL output (one frame per line)
  -l, --labels string     label selector: k=v,k2!=v,'k in (a,b)'
      --limit int         row/line cap per env (default 1000 rows / 500 lines)
      --llmhelp           agent-oriented help for this command (no config or server needed)
      --reason string     why (optional on reads, required on writes)
  -F, --set stringArray   connector flag key=value (repeatable)
      --since string      time window, e.g. 1h, 1d
      --skill string      skill directory (uses <dir>/config.yaml)
      --timeout string    per-target timeout and hard kill (default: system > env > global limits.timeout > 10s); reads estimated above it are refused

Use "tmvp [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## tmvp code
```text
Code Mode: an agent sends one program; it calls tmvp operations (Promise.all,
loops) and only the final value comes back. Every call goes through the tmvp
server like a CLI call: read-only, cost guard (too_expensive), env-type
protection and the audit log (tmvp logs) all apply.

  tmvp code operations                      # db.query, db.describe, ...
  tmvp code describe db.query
  tmvp code run prog.js --json              # {ok, value, error, ms}
  tmvp code run stuck-orders                # <skill dir>/scripts/stuck-orders.js
  tmvp code scripts                         # saved scripts + first-line description
  tmvp code check prog.js                   # diagnostics, nothing runs (exit 2 on errors)

  const r = await Promise.all(["dev","staging","prod"].map(env =>
    ops.db.query({ env, args: ["select count(*) as n from orders"] })))

Operations take {env, args[], flags{}, labels, diff, limit, since, timeout, reason};
env accepts what the CLI selector accepts (dev, dev,prod, all, prod*, type:prod).
Results are {rows, lines, targets, errors, exit}. A refused call throws with
the tmvp code first (policy_blocked: ..., too_expensive: ...).
Writes are write.<system>.<verb> {env, args, reason, preview, force}; they
need --allow-writes and still go through the server write path.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the program failed, 2 nothing ran (check errors, usage).
Scripts never hold secrets: credentials stay in config.yaml secret references.

Usage:
  tmvp code <run|check|capabilities|describe|operations|docs|skill|scripts> [args] [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-writes        let write.<system>.<verb> run (server still requires reason, one env, force on protected envs)
      --concurrency int     tmvp operations in flight at once (default 4)
  -h, --help                help for code
      --input input         JSON value the program reads as the global input
      --max-memory int      soft Go memory limit in MiB for this process (best effort: a runaway program fails instead of exhausting the machine); 0 = off (default 1024)
      --max-ops int         tmvp operation calls per program; past it the program stops (uncatchable, exit 1) (default 200)
      --max-steps int       program step budget (statements + calls + loop iterations) (default 1000000)
      --max-time duration   wall-clock budget for the whole program (default 1m0s)
```

## tmvp secrets
```text
Manage and check the server's in-memory secrets for this product

Usage:
  tmvp secrets [command]

Available Commands:
  audit       Secret fetches/refreshes/invalidations/failures from the audit log: name, time, triggering command (no values)
  clear       Drop this product's secrets and connections from server memory
  reload      Re-run every secret command (after rotation); prints names + ok/failed
  status      Per secret: ok|missing|invalid|login_required, source tool, last fetch, value changed, expiry, cert days left (never values)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for secrets
```

## tmvp server
```text
The local tmvp server (auto-started by every call)

Usage:
  tmvp server [command]

Available Commands:
  run         Run the server in the foreground (what auto-start launches)
  start       Start the server detached (normally automatic)
  status      Loaded products, connections, tunnels, secret slots (names only)
  stop        Stop the server (drops all secrets and connections)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for server
```

## tmvp skill
```text
Product skill: add <name> <type>, sync (SKILL.md from config), lint; install (shipped skills like tmvp-discoverer)

Usage:
  tmvp skill [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Add a system to config.yaml (comments and order kept) and create assets/<name>/
  install     Install the tmvp-discoverer skill (opt-in) into ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills and $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills; then ask your agent: /tmvp-discoverer. Later tmvp runs keep installed copies current
  lint        Check skill structure: SKILL.md front-matter, config validates, no secret values, saved items have front-matter, asset paths exist
  sync        Regenerate SKILL.md from config.yaml (deterministic; hand-written SKILL.md is left alone)

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for skill
```

## tmvp verbs
```text
List connector verbs so an agent can discover them at runtime.

  read        plain tmvp <env> <system> <verb>
  write       only tmvp write <env> <system> <verb> --reason "..."
  destructive write that also needs destructive: true
  read-write  runs both ways; mutates only through tmvp write
  default     the write verb used when tmvp write gets a non-verb (e.g. raw SQL)
  @item       the verb a bare "tmvp <env> <system> @name" runs

Usage:
  tmvp verbs [type...] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for verbs
```

Usage:
  tmvp version [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for version
```

error: runtime: requires at least 2 arg(s), only received 1
exit status 1

opensearch   mapping        read                   mapping <index> — one row per field: index, field (dotted), type
opensearch   search         read [@item]           search <index> '<json>'|@saved [-F q=<lucene>] — hits as rows; size ≤ --limit, server timeout; @saved = queries/<name>.json (front-matter index:)
opensearch   count          read                   count <index> ['<json>'|@saved] [-F q=<lucene>]
opensearch   cat            read                   cat <endpoint> [pattern] — allow-listed _cat endpoints: health indices aliases nodes shards allocation count segments thread_pool pending_tasks recovery templates master plugins fielddata tasks
opensearch   get            read                   get <index> <id> — one document
opensearch   index          write [default]        index <index> '<json>'|@saved [-F id=<id>] — create/replace a document
opensearch   update         write                  update <index> <id> '<partial json>' — partial update (body without "doc"/"script" is wrapped in {"doc": …})
opensearch   delete         write                  delete <index> <id> — delete one document
opensearch   update-by-query write                  update-by-query <index> '<json with query + script>' (--preview = count; no query = every doc → needs destructive)
opensearch   delete-index   destructive            delete-index <index> — no wildcards, no _all
opensearch   delete-by-query destructive            delete-by-query <index> '<json with query>' (--preview = count)
opensearch   reindex        destructive            reindex '<json {"source":…,"dest":…}>'
portforward  ls             read                   ls — what this hop reaches: remote, via chain, local listener (no dial)
portforward  status         read                   dial the remote through the tunnel; latency, listener
portforward  open           read                   open a local 127.0.0.1 listener on local_port: or the tmvp port convention (= export pg-service) [-F port=N] (kept while the server keeps the system warm)
portforward  close          read                   close the local listener
postgres     ls             read                   ls — saved queries (@name, all asset roots) then live tables, views, matviews
postgres     health         read                   ping, server version, recovery state, latency
postgres     describe       read                   describe            → tables; describe <table> → columns
postgres     query          read [@item]           query "<sql>" [params...] | query @saved [params...] (read-only tx, row cap)
postgres     exec           write [default]        exec "<sql>"|@saved [params...] (tmvp write; --preview = rolled-back tx)
prometheus   ls             read                   ls [substring] — metric names (label __name__ values), filtered by substring, capped by --limit
prometheus   query          read                   query "<promql>" [-F time=RFC3339] — instant vector → one row per series
prometheus   range          read                   range "<promql>" [-F step=30s] — over --since (default 1h, ≤7d), one row per sample
prometheus   alerts         read                   alerts — active alerts (name, state, severity, since)
redis        ls             read                   ls [-F sep=:] — key prefixes from a bounded SCAN sample (≤5000 keys), with counts and dbsize
redis        info           read                   info [section] → key/value rows
redis        get            read                   get <key> (string values; other types → use type)
redis        scan           read                   scan [pattern] [-F type=hash] (bounded SCAN, never KEYS)
redis        ttl            read                   ttl <key>
redis        type           read                   type <key>
redis        set            write                  set <key> <value> [ttl e.g. 10m]
redis        del            write                  del <key> [key...] (literal keys, no patterns)
redis        expire         write                  expire <key> <ttl e.g. 1h>
redis        flushdb        destructive            flushdb (destructive)
redis        flushall       destructive            flushall (destructive)
script       ls             read                   ls — saved scripts across all asset roots: name, read|write, source file
script       list           read                   list — alias of ls
script       run            read [@item]           run @name [args] — only scripts declared `# tmvp: read`
script       exec           write [default]        exec @name [args] — any script (tmvp write; --preview shows it)
ssh          ls             read                   ls — saved scripts across all asset roots: @name, read|write, description, source; plus running containers (name, image, status, ports)
ssh          health         read                   connect, uname, uptime, latency
ssh          docker         read                   docker ps [-a] | logs <c> [--tail N] [--since X] [--timestamps] | inspect <c> (env masked) | stats [c] | top <c> | images | compose ps | compose logs <svc> (-F project=<dir> | -F file=<path>) — allow-list only
ssh          script         read [@item]           script @name [args...] [-F container=<c>] — saved script declared read (assets/<system>/scripts/<name>.sh); in a container via docker exec -i
ssh          run            write [default]        run "<command>"|@name [args...] [-F container=<c>] (tmvp write; nice + timeout + output caps; in a container via docker exec)
web          login          read                   login [-F user=ops] — run the scripted login (manual: browser → tmvp login <env> <system>)
web          goto           read                   goto <page|/path> — navigate (base_url + path)
web          text           read                   text <el|page.el> — visible text of an element
web          snapshot       read                   snapshot [el] — accessibility snapshot (refs e1, e2 ...)
web          screenshot     read                   screenshot [el] — PNG under ~/.tmvp/<product>/web/shots
web          check          read                   check [page|--all] — run the page checks
web          ls             read                   ls — declared pages across all asset roots (path, elements, actions, source); offline
web          pages          read                   pages — declared pages, paths, actions
web          elements       read                   elements <page> — declared elements, locators, mutating/never
web          click          read-write             click <el> — read: non-mutating elements in destructive envs; else tmvp write ... click <el> --reason
web          fill           read-write             fill <el> <value> — as click (value never on argv)
web          press          read-write             press <key> — always mutating (may submit): tmvp write ... press <key> --reason
web          select         read-write             select <el> <value> — as click
web          do             read-write [default]   do <action> [k=v ...] — page action; mutating ones via tmvp write (--preview resolves only)
```
